- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to compensate for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, model is lagging; increase forecast by 0.5–1% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model exhibits oscillation bias; smooth forecast by averaging 3-day moving average of true and forecast values.
